note: The check suite runs ONLY checks registered here (founding spec §4).
Registration requires an admission record: the named defect the check
caught or the contract it uniquely carries, the licensing issue, and a
removal signal declared at birth. An unregistered check file is dead
code; one meta check asserts the registry and the checks/ tree agree.
Every removal signal names its observing instrument (kogaki#113):
removal_instrument is `act: <the act that already happens and owes the
removal row>`, `none: <why no act in this repository can observe it>`,
or `probe: <tree-local shell predicate>` (exit 0 = the signal's
condition now holds; exit 1 = not yet; anything else = the probe could
not establish). Probes are evaluated by check-registry-conformance.sh,
which renders candidates report-only — removal stays a judgment.
Every admission record carries RE-EXECUTABLE EFFICACY EVIDENCE
(kogaki#243). The named defect above is a claim about what this check
CATCHES, and registration used to take it on the author's word —
constrain-generation applied to check EXISTENCE, never to check
EFFICACY. `efficacy` names the counterfactual instead: the case that
CONSTRUCTS the named defect and asserts the check REFUSES it.
`case: <path>::<verbatim label>` — the payload is the path, `::`,
and the label, WITH NOTHING APPENDED; human prose goes in the
sibling `efficacy_note`, on the convention `runtime_ms_note` sets.
`none: <why no counterfactual exists in this tree>` — the honest
state, and it is a MEASUREMENT rather than a deferral marker.
check-registry-conformance.sh refuses a `case:` unless <path> exists
and contains <label> literally and EXACTLY ONCE. What that buys,
claimed precisely because overstating it would be the very defect
kogaki#243 names: editing or deleting the cited text breaks the entry
that cites it, and a label too generic to identify one case is
refused as non-unique. What it does NOT decide: that the cited text
is a COMPLETE case label rather than part of one, or that it occurs
in code rather than in a comment. Both are judgments about meaning,
and a language-aware parser for them would be a lint over judgment.
Shape and resolution are gated; whether the counterfactual is a GOOD
one is judgment and is never gated — the split `probe:` runs under.
A member that DELEGATES its assertions to another artifact's fixture
pass carries `case_floor` (kogaki#661). Such a member can verify that
the pass RAN CLEAN and cannot, by the same evidence, verify that the
pass STILL ASSERTS ANYTHING: an exit code and an output token both
IMPROVE as the cases disappear, so both survive the deletion of every
one. Measured at kogaki#659 — a pass reporting `0 case(s) pass` exits 0
and prints its own token. `case_floor` is the minimum count the pass
must report. THE COMPARISON RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (kogaki#970): below
the floor the member FAILS because cases were LOST, and ABOVE it the
member FAILS because cases were ADDED and the floor was not advanced in
the same act.
THE ORIGINAL GROUND FOR A FLOOR RATHER THAN AN EXACT COUNT IS AMENDED
HERE RATHER THAN SILENTLY CONTRADICTED. It read: `a floor rather than an
exact count, because asserting the exact number turns every legitimate
new case into a failing check, which is the pressure that gets the
assertion deleted.` That was a real objection and it was about FRICTION,
so it is answered at the friction rather than dismissed: the upward
refusal names the exact one-line registry edit that discharges it, so a
sitting that adds a case is told what to do in the same breath as being
stopped, and the edit lands in the commit that added the case.
WHAT THE ONE-SIDED FLOOR COST, measured rather than argued (kogaki#970):
`terrain-runtime` declared 83 against a pass reporting 96. `N < FLOOR` is
green for every N above the floor, so the 13-case gap was undetectable —
any case inside it could have been deleted and the member would still
have passed. Six of the eight members declaring a floor sat exactly at
it and two had drifted, and nothing in the suite could tell those two
states apart. A ratchet advanced by hand at some increments and not
others is a ratchet that stops holding.
THE DECREMENT GATE BELOW IS UNTOUCHED, and mechanizing the increment
ratifies no new authority: the owner ruling of 2026-08-26 already made an
increment free, so what changed is that a free act is now also a
REQUIRED one. The rule is carried by check-registry-conformance.sh's
`validate_floor_exceeds_arm`, which is stated over the DECLARATION rather
than the delegating class — a member declaring a floor owes both arms —
so member N+1 is covered by the rule and not by a list somebody
remembered to extend.
It is REQUIRED of any registered check whose file spawns another
artifact's self-test, and that class is DETECTED rather than
enumerated: the dispatch shape is what conformance matches, so member
N+1 is covered by the match and not by a list somebody remembered to
extend.
LOWERING `case_floor` IS AN ADMISSION-CLASS CHANGE (owner ruling
2026-08-26). Without this the field is the silent-shrinkage channel one
hop removed: deleting a case goes red while decrementing the floor
beside it goes green. So a decrement owes a paired `case_floor_note`
naming the case(s) retired, and check-registry-conformance.sh DENIES an
unpaired decrement — deny rather than report, at the same strictness an
incomplete admission record already draws, because the ruling's own
terms are that a decrement needs the same review path as admitting a
member. The comparison reads the floor at the base commit, resolved on
the idiom check-consult-receipts.sh already uses; where no base
resolves, the row renders CANNOT-DETERMINE and never a pass — an
absent input owes could-not-establish rather than the healthy-looking
answer an absent-reads-as-unchanged coercion produces (kogaki#116).
An INCREMENT is free and owes nothing: adding cases is the direction
the floor exists to protect.
WHERE THE COUNT IS READ FROM is fixed here, because four members cite this
note for it (kogaki#661, AC10). The contract on the PASS is that it emits a
NON-NEGATIVE INTEGER count its own member can locate; the EXTRACTION is the
MEMBER'S OWN, declared in that member's file. Deliberately not one grammar
imposed on every runtime: the delegating passes print their counts three
different ways today — `terrain self-test: 18 case(s) pass`, `cite-check
self-test: 15 case(s) pass` and `fixture pass: 10/10 owner-register cases`
— and unifying them would make a decision about check plumbing get paid for
by edits to three unrelated runtimes. A member that cannot locate a count in
its pass's output FAILS: an unreadable floor is not a pass, on the same
ground as a base that will not resolve.
STILL OPEN, named rather than left: a member whose pass prints no parseable
figure at all. All four print one today; deciding what such a member owes is
its own act (deferred slot `delegating-member-with-no-parseable-count`).
OPTIONAL PER-ENTRY KEY `serial: true` (kogaki#789). The suite runs its
members CONCURRENTLY and prints the log in registry order; an entry that
cannot share the working tree with another member declares `serial: true`
and is run alone, before the pool. NO MEMBER DECLARES IT TODAY, and the
absence is a reading rather than an oversight: `runs-retention` and
`registry-conformance` are the only members touching shared paths and both
only READ them. `CHECKS_JOBS=1` in the environment restores fully serial
execution for a whole run. Neither switch changes what any member checks or
what the log says — the runner's own header carries the argument.

admission.contract:
registry/tree agreement, both ways (an unregistered check file is dead code, a registered file that does not exist is a dangling entry), plus admission-shape validation: every registered entry carries a non-empty admission record — the contracts this file's own note declares and nothing else carries.

PLUS the DELEGATING-MEMBER FLOOR (kogaki#661, story 1.92): a member whose file spawns another artifact's fixture pass owes `case_floor`, and the class is DETECTED by dispatch shape rather than enumerated, so member N+1 is covered by the match. The floor's own edit is gated in one direction only — a DECREMENT owes a paired `case_floor_note` and is DENIED without one, at the strictness an incomplete admission record draws, because lowering a floor is an admission-class change (owner ruling 2026-08-26); an INCREMENT owes nothing. An unresolvable base renders CANNOT-DETERMINE and never a pass. Declared limit, carried in the check's own words beside the pattern: the match is over TEXT, so a file merely CONTAINING the dispatch shape is indistinguishable from one that runs it — the same boundary `efficacy` declares between code and comment, and the same refusal of a language-aware parser as a lint over judgment.

PLUS the REGISTERING-MEMBER DESCRIBED-CASE RULE (kogaki#990): a member that registers its cases by id owes a `contract` that describes each one, and the class is DETECTED by the registration call rather than enumerated, so member N+1 is covered by the match exactly as it is for the delegating class above. An id is described by `(<id>)` or by `(<stem>)`, its leading run of letters, and BOTH spellings are admitted because the two vocabularies differ by design — a registration id disambiguates where a reused letter cannot, while `contract` speaks in letters; requiring the LITERAL id fired on 13 of one member's 35 ids at the head this entered on, every one of them described, which is a false red on the naming convention rather than on an omission. A member registering no cases is outside the class, and an EMPTY contract is left to the incomplete-record failure above rather than double-reported here. Declared limit, carried beside the pattern in the check's own words: this file is inside the set its own pattern searches, so the registration call is named in prose WITHOUT its argument parentheses — the rule's first run reported THIS member as registering a case it does not have. What it does not prove, stated rather than implied: that a clause says the RIGHT thing about its case. A mention is mechanically checkable and adequacy is not, so the rule refuses the SILENCE and never grades the prose — and it inherits the registering member's own blind side, since a case with no registration site is invisible to both. THE PATTERN READS ALL THREE QUOTED SPELLINGS of the registration call and names the fourth shape as a THIRD declared limit: a call taking a variable registers an id that is not in the text, so no reader of the text can recover it (PR #1000 round 1).

PLUS the IMPLEMENT-LANE DECLARATION'S SHAPE (kogaki#1188): `.claude/implement-lane.json` is git-ignored (`.gitignore` line 79), so a fresh clone and every `git worktree add` run without one -- that absence is REPORTED, as a typed `implement-lane:` row, and never FAILS. When the file IS present, `suite_runner` must be a non-empty string naming a file that exists in this tree; anything else (absent key, empty string, a name resolving to no file, or JSON this member cannot parse) FAILS by name. What this does not decide: whether the named runner behaves as `suite_runner` promises -- that is the runner's own registered check's claim, not this one's.

admission.contract: the consult-first discipline's reading act: reports the branch's consulted: receipt count and distinct pins, rendering zero explicitly — an obligation generates no event to hook, so observability is the whole remedy. Fails only on a malformed receipt, never on the count. Fenced-block quotations are MENTIONS of the grammar, not receipts, and are excluded from the counted set (kogaki#41, the PR #40 false positive). Parses the v2 continuation block (kogaki#28, story 1.10) — request_id, outcome, one query line per framing, indented under line one, all OPTIONAL so every v1 receipt in git history stays valid — and widens malformed to SIX field defects, all conformance rather than counting: an outcome outside the hub's ratified triple (a bare `miss` collapses the two causes the 2026-08-02 correction separated), a re-framed outcome recording fewer than every framing's query, an `uncovered-after-N` whose N disagrees with the number of query lines recorded (shape validation alone let a receipt claim seven framings while recording two), an N below the two-framing floor (a miss is not recordable as uncovered until re-asked along another axis; the floor is stated as its own clause because it is currently also implied by the query rule, and an implied invariant is one a refactor drops unnoticed), and a PARTIAL v2 receipt — continuations stay optional so a v1 receipt is valid, but once ANY continuation is present the receipt owes all three fields SPEC §4 requires (PR #43 review). The embedded fixture pass is the discrimination evidence, run every invocation, and asserts the PARSED FIELDS rather than only counts — a count-only assertion cannot observe whether the continuation fields were read at all, which measured 2 of 8 v2 cases discriminating before the assertion was widened and 6 of 8 after. States what it does NOT verify: the query-count rule is satisfied by two rephrasings of one question, and axis-variation is a judgment no count can observe — the check asserts the framings were RECORDED and routes whether they differed to the review lane, with a receipt found carrying two rephrasings as the observation that would earn a real detector. Empty values are handled by ONE rule applied in the parse: continuation PRESENCE is recorded as a fact about the text rather than inferred from value truthiness, and an empty value is absent for every field alike — before which empty query lines counted as recorded framings, so `uncovered-after-3-framings` with three blank queries satisfied N == len() (PR #43 re-review), and a `query:` line holding a SERIALIZED TOOL ARGUMENT rather than a question (kogaki#160 finding 4): the field is defined at the consultation map's Miss-postmortem field as the question verbatim, the grammar accepted any non-empty value, and `query: {"tag":"lessons/claude-code-ops"}` shipped on master passing every clause above — because the transport DERIVED the line, reading it off policy_lookup's own `question` argument and falling back to the raw --args JSON for every other tool, so a gloss_index consult had no field in which to record its question. gateway-query.mjs now requires `--question` per `--args` and refuses without it, making the emission unproducible on the tool path; this clause is the floor under condition 2's marked-exception path, and is the narrowest rule that discriminates — a value that is a JSON object/array end to end is a tool argument, while a question CONTAINING braces or quotes passes, with fixtures in both directions. Backward compatible by the scan window: this check reads merge-base..HEAD plus the PR body, never a file on the default branch and never the whole history, so receipts already merged lie outside every future scan and no branch fails on work it did not author. THE SECOND AXIS (kogaki#268): a `disposition:` continuation key carrying the GATE half — what the gate did with the consultation — on its own field rather than in `outcome:`, which is where the digest's vocabulary claim assumed it lived and where this check's own ratified-triple clause refuses it. Three vocabularies in this seam are called `outcome` and two of them are mutually exclusive in one slot, so the resolution is one field per axis, each owned by whoever must agree on it: the values are ADOPTED verbatim from the ratified closed two-value set (`auto-resolved-FYI | escalated`, spec-policy-fork-consultation §"Amended 2026-07-21 (triage, #519)", "no consumer-local extension") because a field read by both sides of the boundary is the boundary's and the boundary's owner is the hub (`topics/knowledge-architecture.md:31@dec0d568`), while the field's SHAPE is this repository's. The key is OPTIONAL and is deliberately NOT added to presence-implies-completeness' owed set: most consults here are not fork gates, and requiring the field would force a value on them. Recognising the key in the checker is a REQUIREMENT rather than a convenience — the continuation scan stops at the first unrecognised indented key, so a receipt carrying `disposition:` above its query lines parsed on the pre-#268 scanner as a field-less v1 line with every later field silently dropped, and 10 of the 12 new fixtures fail that scanner spliced against this fixture table. What it does NOT make substantiable, stated rather than implied: `consult-miss` and `degraded` stay uncountable from receipts under this or any schema — an unconsulted fork emits no receipt and a degraded consult emits none by design — so both are refused as values with that reason named, and the report line counts the two dispositions and says what nothing here can count WIDENED (kogaki#336): the grammar gains a THIRD continuation key, `axis:`, and it is the first that binds PER QUERY — upward to the nearest preceding `query:`, first declaration wins, an axis before any query orphaned and reported. The check validates SHAPE ONLY — position and a non-empty token — because the `subject | conduct` value set is the hub's to ratify under the boundary-field rule (product-lab@4cc496b topics/knowledge-architecture.md:50), so any value passes and unknown ones are reported and denied nowhere; the report NAMES the distinct axes rather than only counting them, which is what makes an unratified set observable while it is unratified. Eight per-query binding cases exercise both directions, plus an explicit never-gates assertion that an unknown axis is not reported malformed — the assertion standing between shape-only and this repository silently minting boundary values it does not own. Runtime re-measured 80 -> 95 ms (three local runs) for the widening rather than for an admission, because the binding quantity is cost per ship-cycle rather than member count.

The composed-form identity cite (kogaki#612): lesson and journey kinds in the join key, a bare sha pin taken as served, an absent or empty pin REFUSING composition rather than minting an unpinned cite, and the positional form unproducible by the composer. The abbreviated-form classification repair (kogaki#653, PR #658): both declaring surfaces admitting the ABNORMAL line `displayIdAbnormalLine` actually emits, with the digit-free tail retained as the CONTROL that the fix is a repair and not a widening. And the §15 control plane (kogaki#652): the shipped workflow table loading under the structural rules, run counts read from a record alone with conditional entries counted separately, and the executor's refusals — no states, a duplicate state id, a kind the executor does not interpret, a write state naming no artifact, a table with no terminal state, a write state with no renderer bound, and an owner input arriving with no outstanding wait. A THIN INVOKER — the cases live with the runtime, seam-free by construction, every case constructing its own inputs so no gateway and no network are reachable. NOT carried here and named so the boundary is legible: survey/cover/figure/navigation composition over records in the tree WAS check-terrain-composition.sh, whose admission record and removal signal were about that contract — that member was REMOVED at kogaki#770 under the 2026-09-02 retention rule, so the contract is carried by nobody and this record states the absence rather than pointing at a deleted file; folding the runtime fixtures into it would put two contracts behind one removal signal. PLUS THE LANE BINDING (kogaki#750): the report record store's DEFAULT destination is `runs/terrain/reports/` in the working tree, the terrain lane resolves under the repository's own runs/ directory, no default resolves under a home directory, and an explicit --report-dir still wins. Read through the PURE `reportsDestination`, split from the preparing `reportsDir` for the reason PR #702 finding 2 gives — a case asserting a default must not create it. admission.contract: the boundary-receipt binding at the merge layer (specs/SPEC.md §4, kogaki#25): a consultation-map boundary whose trigger terms MATCH the branch, with ZERO receipts present, FAILS — which is what converts the map from advice an agent may remember into a carrier that binds on every PR. A PRESENCE CHECK OVER TWO DECLARED ENUMERATIONS (the map's entries, the branch's receipts), both named in the output because a coverage claim is a fraction OF an enumeration. It NEVER BRANCHES ON THE OUTCOME TOKEN and structurally cannot: it reads line one only, so `discriminating`, `covered-after-reframing` and `uncovered-after-N-framings` satisfy it alike — the obligation is TO ASK and never TO HAVE FOUND (as corrected for kogaki#32), and a check that passed on some outcomes and failed on others would be judging whether the consultation SUCCEEDED, which is the review lane's property. LINE ONE ONLY also keeps it independent of the v2 continuation block (kogaki#28, story 1.10), whose validation stays with check-consult-receipts.sh — that check's report-never-gate contract is not absorbed, redefined or deleted, because this one gates a DIFFERENT property. It BINDS PRESENCE, NOT ORDER: a receipt written after the code it should have preceded satisfies it exactly as one written before, nothing in this repository observes that ordering, and the gap is stated rather than assumed covered (observed live on the story-1.10 branch). THE ATTRIBUTION HALF IS CARRIER-LESS AND MARKED: line one names a pin, never a boundary, so one receipt satisfies every matched boundary and a PR touching two while consulting one passes — carrier-less by omission is the defect, carrier-less with a reopen trigger is admissible (topics/knowledge-architecture.md:52@ed47fbd). FALSE POSITIVES ARE ACCEPTED AND DISCHARGED rather than narrowed away: an incidental term match is answered by the same act a real one asks for, so a spurious match costs one consultation rather than a false verdict — the map's ratified accretion polarity preserved at gate severity (owner decision at implementation; narrowing to diff paths alone was considered and declined as a silent shrink of what the map binds). THE SOURCE SET IS DECLARED and so is what it could not read — diff paths, changed text (commit messages, PR body), and the linked issue body, with an unavailable source NAMED rather than passed over, since an instrument that reports absence without establishing it is the defect the review lane refuses one layer up (carried by the engine since kogaki#630 retired check-review-report.sh with the stack); an unreadable or unparseable map is COULD NOT ESTABLISH and fails, in its own wording, because a fallback worded as a finding accuses. The embedded fixture pass runs every invocation and needs no network, firing BOTH discriminating cases — matched+receipt passes, matched+none fails — plus source coverage, outcome-invariance, line-one-only, use-vs-mention, and the word-bound case that keeps short terms from matching inside longer words. AND THE PATH SET IS THE BRANCH'S OWN, COMPUTED AT THE FORK POINT (kogaki#264): CI supplies `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` — the base branch's TIP at event time — and `git diff A..B` is a tree diff rather than a range, so every file that landed on master after this branch forked entered the path set and matched a boundary, at DENY severity, naming a file the branch never touched; the neighbouring `git log` and `git rev-list` read the same string as a genuine range, so the report printed a truthful commit count beside a path set of a different span. Paths, commits and count now all read the FORK POINT's span, and the output NAMES the fork point and says when the supplied base has advanced past it. The repair is sited in the check and not in the workflow because `base.sha` is a truthful name for a truthful value whose other consumers read it only through range operators, and because no fixture in this repository can watch a YAML expression.
